for those of you who have seen ratatouille, one of the great questions in the ai age: are we remy or linguini?

are the humans in control of the combined entity (we are remy), or are the ai in control and we are simply the meat proxies (we are linguini)?

our vision with muse is undeniably the former—we are remy! we have big dreams and goals, many of which may not be appropriate for our station or our exact starting condition. but that doesn't matter—we dream like a rat who wants to be a michelin-starred chef in paris.

muse is our partner to help make that happen. ultimately, we are pulling the hairs (?), and it is our vision that ends up on the plate (?), but over time we will accomplish things that we could not do without muse.

(obviously this metaphor is super confusing because i'm saying the humans are the rat, but if you watched the movie you catch my drift)

anyway this whole mini-essay was just to justify my shitpost—pls enjoy

note_tweet.text:
We’re exploring how AI can accelerate health science research.

While AI has made significant breakthroughs in formal sciences like mathematics, health data science depends on imperfect real-world data and consequential choices about cohorts, variables, and causal assumptions.

To explore how AI can assist health researchers, we built a human-led research scaffold powered by Muse Spark 1.3 and Muse Wonder with access to 5M retrospective de-identified electronic health records and publicly available data. A cohort of medical experts used the system to conduct original research, accelerate hypothesis generation, code execution, and manuscript drafting while maintaining full authority over scientific decisions.

Today, we’re sharing 10 research manuscripts produced through this exploration, spanning cardiology, oncology, infectious disease, emergency medicine, and more.

Read more in our research blog: https://t.co/26l6Du6vIk

We benchmarked Gemini 4 Argon, Muse Wonder, and Muse Spark comprehensively on hard document OCR tasks.

They're all pretty good! 
- Muse Spark and Gemini 4 Argon* are SOTA at their respective price points for table understanding among frontier models. 
- Wonder and Argon are also quite good at chart understanding, reading order, and formatting recognition

It's exciting that frontier models are starting to ramp up on visual understanding capabillities. 

We're committed to open benchmarking of all available models even as we aim to build the best specialized models for document parsing and extraction. 

You can check out the full set of models on OpenDocRouter: https://t.co/v8PieWWUNV

If you want a dedicated OCR solution without choosing, come check out LlamaParse: https://t.co/XYZmx5TFz8

note_tweet.text:
The two top models on the Intelligence Index take about twice as long per task: Claude Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 (@AnthropicAI) vs. Muse Wonder (@Meta).

Muse Wonder finishes an average task in 6.8 minutes with a 52.4 score. Opus 5.5 takes 13.2 and Sonnet 5.5 takes 15.3, scoring 57.6 and 56.0. Muse Spark 1.3 and GPT-6 Astra (@OpenAI) follow at 8.1.

When someone is waiting on the answer, minutes can matter more than a few index points. Merge Gateway lets you send latency-sensitive requests to the fast model and the hard ones to the strong one, behind one endpoint.

Scores via https://t.co/TeTHwS52d4, week of Oct 12.
